identity.title: Pressurizer Safety Valve Lift Setpoint Drifted Outside of Technical Specification Tolerance

cause.proximate_text: The cause of the PSV lift setting being outside of the TS allowed tolerance is a personnel error that resulted in inadvertent installation of a PSV that had previously demonstrated a significant amount of setpoint drift.
cause.theme: personnel error - failure to retire known-drift-prone valve from service

nodes.proximate_text: The cause of the PSV lift setting being outside of the TS allowed tolerance is a personnel error that resulted in inadvertent installation of a PSV that had previously demonstrated a significant amount of setpoint drift.

nodes.display_name: PSV with known drift history not retired from service
nodes.description: Corrective action from March 2015 investigation to retire the PSV was not implemented due to personnel error.
The PSV was inadvertently reinstalled in the 2016 fall refueling outage with an acceptable lift setting despite its known drift history.

nodes.display_name: PSV lift setpoint drifted outside TS tolerance
nodes.description: Upon testing on April 29, 2021, 1RC-123 was found with a lift setting of -1.3% from setpoint, outside the TS allowed tolerance of +/-1%.

nodes.display_name: PSV lift setting outside TS tolerance - reportable condition prohibited by Technical Specifications

properties.note: As-found lift setting -1.3% vs TS allowed tolerance +/-1%; safety analysis assumes +/-3% tolerance, so condition had no actual safety significance.

nodes.display_name: Replace PSV 1RC-123 with spare PSV confirmed within tolerance

chain: personnel error - corrective action to retire drift-prone PSV not implemented [cause TBD] -> PSV inadvertently reinstalled in 2016 outage -> PSV lift setpoint drifts further over time -> found at -1.3% during 2021 refueling outage test, outside TS +/-1% tolerance -> reportable condition prohibited by TS (no actual safety significance; within +/-3% safety analysis basis)
